recent_reviews.disliked: It may once have deserved a 4-star rating, but not currently. The facilities are quite old. In addition, small courtesies that are nice to have are missing, such as providing a bottle of water or body cream in the room. The lighting is extremely scarce; it is even disconcerting. Acceptable overall, but I would not repeat it.

recent_reviews.liked: In the city center, a few steps from the city's points of interest. The hotel's view over the slope of the Rio Corgo is spectacular. Comfortable bed and room temperature.
recent_reviews.disliked: Poor soundproofing of the rooms. Materials very worn and outdated. It already requires renovation. Breakfast has little variety, not taking the opportunity to showcase regional products.

recent_reviews.liked: The furniture had a lot of dust, which means the cleaning was not very good.
Cleanliness, the staff, the location, and the delicious breakfast.
recent_reviews.disliked: One single drawback: the presence of a group of girls from a football club who disrupted part of the evening and continued until 12:30 AM despite my reminders to keep order; that is the only unpleasant point.

recent_reviews.liked: We generally liked everything. Central hotel with a comfortable, clean room, with working air conditioning and good Wi-Fi. We recommend it.

decision_a.overall_risk_rationale: Occupancy and revenue metrics fell sharply in the 4-week window (occupancy and RevPAR down ~71%, TRevPAR down ~82%), while reviews point to recurring operational issues (facility condition, cleanliness, breakfast, noise). The combination of weak commercial performance and repeated service/maintenance complaints poses a high business risk if not addressed.
decision_a.executive_summary: Immediate priorities are to stabilise commercial performance (recover occupancy/revenue), and address operational and physical-plant issues that appear repeatedly in guest feedback: outdated/worn rooms and poor lighting, housekeeping lapses, limited breakfast variety, and noise/soundproofing problems. Preserve strengths (central location, river view, hospitable staff, comfortable beds, Wi‑Fi and on-site amenities) and use them in targeted short-term offers while implementing a phased capital and operational improvement plan.

priorities.problem: Occupancy and revenue per available room have dropped steeply (occupancy -71.6%, RevPAR -71.3%, TRevPAR -81.9%) in the decision window.
priorities.recommended_action: Immediate revenue-management review: audit pricing and channel mix, apply short-term tactical discounts or packages to stimulate bookings, push targeted promotions highlighting strengths (central location, river view, free parking, indoor pool), pursue group/corporate bookings and local market demand, monitor distribution costs. Coordinate with marketing to promote small immediate service improvements (e.g., complimentary bottled water) to increase conversion. Review cancellation and minimum-stay rules for flexibility in low-demand periods.
priorities.rationale: A rapid commercial response can reduce the short-term revenue shock while operational improvements are planned. Using clear strengths in promotions helps attract guests despite some negative comments about facilities.

priorities.area: Property condition / Capital works & room comfort
priorities.problem: Several reviews describe worn/outdated materials, poor lighting and a general sense that the hotel no longer meets its 4-star expectations.
priorities.recommended_action: Commission a rapid property-condition audit to prioritise fixes (lighting, worn furnishings, visible wear). Create a phased refurbishment plan (short-term cosmetic refreshes and mid-term capital works). In the immediate term, implement low-cost mitigations: add bedside and desk lamps, replace heavily worn textiles, supply small in-room amenities (bottled water, body cream) to improve perceived quality while planning larger works.
priorities.rationale: Guest comments indicate the physical condition undermines the perceived star level. A phased approach manages capital outlay while quickly improving guest perception through targeted, visible interventions.

priorities.problem: At least one guest reported visible dust on furniture and poor cleaning; inconsistent cleanliness undermines guest satisfaction.
priorities.recommended_action: Run immediate housekeeping deep-clean of rooms and public areas. Audit current cleaning processes and checklists, retrain or reallocate housekeeping teams, increase room inspection frequency and implement a short-term audit (random room checks with documented scores). Communicate improvements to guests (e.g., visible inspection tags, welcome note confirming deep-clean). Track housekeeping KPIs (room inspection pass rate, time to rectify issues).
priorities.rationale: Cleanliness is a basic expectation; visible lapses produce negative reviews and reduce repeat business. Quick operational fixes are feasible and visible to guests.

priorities.problem: Some guests find breakfast has little variety and is not taking the opportunity to showcase regional products, though other guests praise the breakfast.
priorities.recommended_action: Review breakfast menu and supplier mix to introduce higher variety and regional items (sampling local cheeses, breads, preserves). Train breakfast staff on presentation and guest engagement. Consider a small menu refresh or rotating special to test guest response. Promote the improved breakfast in marketing communications and booking channels.
priorities.rationale: Improving and differentiating breakfast can increase perceived value and convert bookings; it leverages local assets and can be implemented quickly with modest cost.

priorities.problem: Guests report poor room soundproofing and at least one incident of a disruptive group creating noise until late (12:30 AM).
priorities.recommended_action: Immediate enforcement of quiet-hours policy and staff training on escalation procedures; document and act on noise complaints promptly. Where feasible, allocate rooms to reduce impact of groups on other guests. Evaluate longer-term investments in soundproofing as part of the property audit. Update booking policies for group reservations (deposits, codes of conduct).
priorities.rationale: Noise/disturbance impacts guest comfort and review scores. Quick policy and staff response can reduce recurrence while structural solutions are evaluated.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Multiple reviews praise the central location and the spectacular view over the slope of the Rio Corgo.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Use location and views as key selling points in marketing and packages while improvements are made to rooms.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Several reviews mention hospitality, efficiency and friendliness of staff.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Preserve and recognise staff performance through training and incentives; leverage staff strengths in guest communications and upsell opportunities.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Guests repeatedly cite comfortable beds, working air conditioning and good Wi‑Fi.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Maintain bedding and HVAC service schedules and the Wi‑Fi reliability while cosmetic/major refurbishments are planned.

strengths_to_preserve.area: Amenities & facilities (indoor pool, parking, accessible features)
strengths_to_preserve.reason: Hotel lists attractive facilities (indoor pool, free parking, accessibility features) that support guest value.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Continue to keep these facilities operational and promoted in sales channels; include amenity benefits in short-term packages.

limitations: Analysis uses only the supplied 4-week window and the provided recent review sample (20 reviews). Broader trends outside this window are not available.
Review comments are qualitative and may reflect experiences of a subset of rooms/guests; they do not by themselves identify the root causes of the sharp occupancy/revenue decline.

Operational detail (housekeeping staffing levels, maintenance backlog, current capital budget) and distribution channel data are not provided; recommendations involving costs or timelines require further internal assessment.
No direct causal link between review content and the documented revenue/occupancy changes can be established from the supplied information; both should be investigated separately.

decision_b.overall_risk_rationale: Business trends show large recent declines in RevPAR and occupancy with declining sentiment and increasing expectation gap, while review evidence points to emerging room-condition friction. Strengths (location, staff, cleanliness) persist, and recent-week movement shows partial reversal, so the situation is concerning but not critical.
decision_b.executive_summary: Preserve clear strengths (location, staff, cleanliness). Primary managerial attention should focus on room-condition and fabric issues (aging materials, lighting, soundproofing, linen odor) because multiple recent reviews and the emerging_negative topic point to expectation failures. Near-term operational fixes and policy reviews (breakfast variety, in-room complimentary items, laundry/detergent practices, guest disturbance enforcement) should be implemented or reviewed quickly. Where evidence suggests potential structural causes (soundproofing, general fabric deterioration) request an inspection/assessment before committing capital.

priorities.area: Room condition / property fabric (lighting, worn materials, general state)
priorities.problem: Guests report ageing/worn facilities, scarce lighting and a general impression that the hotel is more dated than expected; this is flagged as an emerging negative topic (room condition) and indicates expectation failure for a 4-star property.
priorities.recommended_action: Commission an immediate managerial inspection of room fabric and public-area finishes to scope the extent of wear (lighting levels, materials, fixtures). Based on the inspection, prepare a phased remediation plan (prioritise safety/guest-impact items). Implement short-term mitigations where feasible (improve lighting intensity/fixtures in affected rooms, replace visibly worn items, communicate clearly about planned remediation). Do not commit to capital expenditure without an inspection and costed assessment.
priorities.rationale: Multiple recent reviews describe aged/worn materials and scarce lighting; 'room condition' is flagged as an emerging negative topic in the context. The problem is likely structural in part and may require phased maintenance or refurbishment; however, inspection is needed to determine scope and cost.

priorities.area: Breakfast offering (variety / showcase of regional products)
priorities.problem: Some guests perceive breakfast as having limited variety and not showcasing regional products, an expectation violation despite other guests praising breakfast.
priorities.recommended_action: Review the breakfast menu and supplier arrangements with the food & beverage team. Evaluate whether adding or rotating regional items or increasing variety can be piloted without large capital outlay. Collect guest preference feedback (e.g., simple survey) during breakfast to confirm demand for regional offerings before implementing lasting changes.
priorities.rationale: Managerial evidence classifies Breakfast as 'positive_with_friction' with an explicit violated expectation week. One recent complaint described limited breakfast variety; however other guests note 'delicious breakfast', indicating an underlying strength to preserve while addressing the specific friction.

priorities.area: In-room complimentary items / basic bathroom provisioning
priorities.problem: At least one guest reported absence of small expected courtesies (bottle of water, body cream), indicating an expectation mismatch around what is provided in-room.
priorities.recommended_action: Review and clarify the in-room provisioning policy (water, basic toiletries). Implement or reinforce a simple housekeeping checklist to ensure consistent delivery of included items; ensure front-desk communications and online descriptions accurately reflect what is provided. If a policy change is considered, evaluate costs and guest-value alignment before adopting.
priorities.rationale: Complaint specifically mentioned missing bottle of water and body cream; managerial evidence for 'bathroom condition' includes an expectation violation week though experience mentions are limited. This appears to be an operational/policy gap that can be addressed without major capital investment.

priorities.area: Housekeeping / laundry practice (linen odor / disinfectant smell)
priorities.problem: At least one guest reported bed linen with a strong smell of disinfectant/detergent, suggesting a possible laundry or product-use issue that can negatively affect perceived cleanliness despite otherwise positive housekeeping mentions.
priorities.recommended_action: Audit laundry and room-cleaning chemical usage and processes (internal or third-party laundry), including product types and concentrations. Trial adjustments or alternative products in a subset of rooms and solicit guest feedback. Retrain housekeeping on drying/ventilation practices where appropriate. If supplied by a vendor, request documentation and quality checks.
priorities.rationale: There is a single explicit complaint about linen odor amid otherwise positive cleanliness mentions. This looks like an operational/process issue that can be investigated and trialed quickly; a focused audit will determine if wider action is required.

priorities.problem: Guests reported both poor soundproofing and disturbance from a noisy group; this combines an operational/policy issue (guest behaviour enforcement, group management) and a possible structural issue (soundproofing).
priorities.recommended_action: Short term: review front-desk and on-site procedures for handling noisy guests and group bookings (quiet-hours messaging, escalation/resolution process). Medium term: schedule a technical assessment of room-to-room and external sound insulation to determine whether remedial works are required. Do not commit to capital works before the assessment.
priorities.rationale: Two recent reviews describe noise issues: one describes poor soundproofing; another describes a disruptive guest group until 00:30 despite reminders. Operational policy changes can reduce recurrence; if the soundproofing assessment shows structural weakness, plan remediation based on scoped findings.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Multiple reviews (and managerial_evidence) consistently praise the hotel's central location and views.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Maintain marketing emphasis on central location; ensure any operational changes (e.g., signage, access) do not reduce perceived convenience.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Several reviews highlight helpful staff and recommend the hotel; managerial_evidence shows staff and service as a clear strength.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Preserve service standards; consider staff briefing on how to communicate short-term remediation actions to guests (e.g., expected improvements, handling noisy groups).

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Managerial evidence shows consistently positive cleanliness mentions across weeks.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Preserve existing housekeeping protocols while auditing specific laundry/chemical practices to address isolated linen-odor reports.

strengths_to_preserve.reason: Guests report comfortable beds, working air conditioning and good Wi‑Fi in multiple reviews.
strengths_to_preserve.management_implication: Maintain current maintenance schedules for HVAC and room amenities; monitor any remediation work to avoid disrupting these strengths.

limitations: Selected complaints (5) are diagnostic examples and may not represent the full review population (total reviews in window = 22). Prevalence should be assessed using full review metadata before major investments.
Evidence identifies several potential structural issues (soundproofing, fabric ageing) but does not provide scope, technical detail, or cost—recommend inspection/assessment before capital decisions.
Some recommendations (e.g., changes to breakfast offering, laundry processes) assume operational feasibility and supplier availability; further internal operational review is required.
Temporal signals show recent reversals in revenue metrics; interpret business trends and customer-experience changes separately and re-evaluate after a new data window.
